links.outcome: Accuracy change when culture-related identifiers/context are inserted into otherwise invariant medical questions
links.effect: Cultural cues significantly affect accuracy (Cochran's Q, p<10^-14), with largest degradation when identifier and context co-occur (up to 3-7 percentage points under option-only prompting); neutral edits produce smaller, non-systematic changes.
links.quote: Across models, cultural cues significantly affect accuracy (Cochran's Q, $p<10^-14$), with the largest degradation when identifier and context co-occur (up to 3-7 percentage points under option-only prompting), while neutral edits produce smaller, non-systematic changes.

screen.reason: Evaluates the robustness/equity of medical LLMs against counterfactual cultural cues across benchmark questions (MedQA variants) without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
